title: Use a district map to show one state’s races on the shapes of its districts, with party told by panel.
rule: Draw the state’s districts in one panel for each party, as Rule 14.7 sets seats on a map, with the margin in steps of one ink, the lightest still a clear fill, and the same steps and key words as the district tile map. Number each district on its shape, or beside it with a leader, and set the national result beside the panels (Rule 14.6).
use_when: The reader asks how close each race was in one state, and the districts’ shapes and places matter.

use_instead.when: Every seat in the country, each the same size
The reader looks up one race’s figures

text: Shapes let a reader find the district where they live, and two panels put each party’s seats together without a party color. Gray steps for the margin keep a close race and a safe one apart on both sides alike.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form district-map: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s80; encode district, party and cls (the margin’s class from clerk-house-results-2024-classes, the table S82 reads); labels.layer the state’s fitted district layer (cd119-mi), labels.fips its code, labels.panels each party’s panel.
